Cholo · PostgreSQL

Every table, query and database program, explained

For each query: what it does, the exact SQL, which button or timer makes it run, the path it takes through the code, what it gives back, and whether it runs inside a transaction. Everything here was traced from the code itself.

51tables (+3 monthly partitions)
260SQL queries in 250 functions
19triggers using 7 trigger functions
5 + 1functions + procedure

How one query gets run

  1. Screen. A React page (in client/src/pages) calls a small API function, for example ridesApi.createRequest().
  2. API call. That function (in client/src/api) sends an HTTP request like POST /api/v1/ride-requests with the login token.
  3. Guards. The route runs checks first: auth (logged in?), requireRole (right kind of user?), validate (is the data correct?).
  4. Controller. Reads the request and calls the service.
  5. Service. Makes the decisions. For anything that changes data it opens a transaction with withTransaction.
  6. Query. A function in server/src/repositories runs the SQL with client.query(sql, [values]).
  7. Back up. PostgreSQL returns { rows, rowCount }. The repository returns the part that's needed (one row, all rows, a count…), the service shapes it, and the controller sends { "success": true, "data": … } as JSON to the screen.

Some queries have no screen at all. Timers run them every few seconds or minutes, and the live connection (Socket.IO) runs them when a driver's phone sends its location.

How to read a query card

Click a card to open it. The coloured labels say what the query does:

READ SELECT · INSERT adds rows · UPDATE changes rows · DELETE removes rows · CALL runs the procedure · LOCK locks rows until COMMIT or ROLLBACK · fn_… uses a database function

Under When it runs, each coloured box is one way the query gets called, from the screen down to the query. The label inside withTransaction means that step is part of a BEGIN … COMMIT.

Words you'll see

WordMeaning
$1, $2Placeholders. The values are sent separately from the SQL text, so nobody can inject SQL through a form (like :name in Oracle).
TransactionA group of statements that all succeed together (COMMIT) or are all undone (ROLLBACK).
FOR UPDATELock the rows you read, so no other transaction can change them until you finish. Others wait their turn.
pg_advisory_xact_lock(n)A lock on a number (like a passenger's id) instead of a row, released at COMMIT or ROLLBACK.
RETURNINGAfter an INSERT or UPDATE, send back columns of the changed row, so no extra SELECT is needed.
AS "camelCase"Renames a column for JavaScript. Double quotes keep the capital letters.
::float8, ::int, ::textType casts (Postgres short form of CAST(x AS …)), so numbers arrive as numbers in JavaScript.
COALESCE(a, b)Use a; if it is NULL use b. Oracle's NVL.
count(*) OVER()The total number of matching rows, added to every row, used to show "page 2 of 5".
ON CONFLICT DO NOTHINGIf the row would break a UNIQUE rule, skip it quietly instead of failing.
set_config('app.user_id', …, true)Stores the acting user's id for this transaction only, so the trip-history trigger can record who made a change.
What the examiner asks for

CSE216 checklist, and where each item is

Checklist itemIn Cholo
Explicit transaction control (COMMIT and ROLLBACK on every DML)Every INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE runs inside withTransaction (BEGIN → COMMIT, or ROLLBACK on any error), in 84 service functions. The token refresh writes BEGIN / COMMIT / ROLLBACK by hand. See all of them.
Triggers (validation, or logging to a shadow table)19 triggers. Logging: fn_log_trip_status writes every trip status change to trip_status_history. Validation: fn_block_mutation refuses edits to money and audit history. Automatic updates: fn_apply_wallet_txn, fn_apply_rating.
Functions (return a computed value)fn_current_pricing, fn_current_commission, fn_wallet_balance_audit, fn_zone_at, fn_point_in_ring.
Procedure (multi-step change to several tables)sp_request_withdrawal: lock the wallet, check the balance, insert the withdrawal, insert the ledger debit (which updates the balance by trigger).
3+ complex queries (several tables and/or aggregates)The 10 analytics reports, getDashboardStats, getRevenueTrend, getTopDrivers, getTopRiders, listUsers, findEligibleDrivers, exportRows, getStatementForMonth…
Appropriate useEach trigger, function and procedure card below has a "Why the database is the right place" paragraph.
Know these answers

Unused tables: payment_methods and invoices are in the design but no query uses them. Monthly statements are built from driver_earnings instead. v_trip_details is also defined but unused.

Rating is updated twice: the trigger trg_apply_rating updates the average, then ratings.refreshAverage recalculates it from all ratings as a safety net.

fn_wallet_balance_audit is only called by the automated tests, as a check that the wallet trigger keeps balances right.

COMMIT and ROLLBACK

Transactions: all or nothing

Think of sending money

Taking 500 taka from you and adding it to your friend are two steps. If the power fails between them, money disappears. A transaction groups them: both happen (COMMIT) or neither does (ROLLBACK).

The helper every service uses: withTransaction

const client = await pool.connect();
Borrow one connection from the pool. Every step of a transaction must use the same connection.
await client.query('BEGIN');
Start the transaction.
const result = await work(client);
Run the service's steps. Each query is given this client, which is what puts it inside the transaction.
await client.query('COMMIT');
Every step worked: save everything permanently.
for (const cb of client.afterCommitCallbacks) cb();
Only now send live messages and notifications, so nobody is told about something that might still be undone.
} catch (error) {
  await client.query('ROLLBACK');
  throw error;
Any step failed: undo every step, then pass the error on so the screen shows a message.
} finally { client.release(); }
Always give the connection back.

server/src/config/db.js:34

What causes a ROLLBACK

  • The service throws an AppError, for example ALREADY_TAKEN when another driver accepted first, or INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS.
  • The database refuses a row: a UNIQUE rule (23505, like two trips for one request), a CHECK rule (23514, like fare parts not adding up) or a foreign key (23503).
  • A trigger or procedure raises an error: fn_block_mutation ("… is append-only") or sp_request_withdrawal ("INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE").
  • Any unexpected crash inside the steps.

The hand-written one: refreshing the login

auth.service.refresh writes BEGIN, COMMIT and ROLLBACK itself. When an old, already-used refresh token shows up, it must COMMIT "cancel this whole session" and still return an error. withTransaction would roll that back. server/src/services/auth.service.js:203

Run automatically by the database

Triggers

Think of a motion-sensor light

Nobody presses a switch. A trigger is code the database runs by itself when a row is inserted, updated or deleted in a certain table. The app can't forget it, because the app doesn't run it.

Trigger words

BEFORE runs before the row is saved: it can change it (NEW.column := …) or refuse it (RAISE EXCEPTION). AFTER runs once the row exists, which is needed to insert a linked row. FOR EACH ROW runs once per changed row. NEW is the row being saved, OLD is the row before an update, and TG_OP is 'INSERT', 'UPDATE' or 'DELETE'. A trigger runs inside the same transaction as the statement that fired it, so a trigger error rolls the whole thing back.

TriggerFiresOn tableRuns function
trg_touch_updated_atBEFORE UPDATE, for each rowusersfn_touch_updated_at
trg_touch_updated_atBEFORE UPDATE, for each rowpassenger_profilesfn_touch_updated_at
trg_touch_updated_atBEFORE UPDATE, for each rowdriver_profilesfn_touch_updated_at
trg_touch_updated_atBEFORE UPDATE, for each rowvehiclesfn_touch_updated_at
trg_touch_updated_atBEFORE UPDATE, for each rowdriver_availabilityfn_touch_updated_at
trg_touch_updated_atBEFORE UPDATE, for each rowwalletsfn_touch_updated_at
trg_touch_updated_atBEFORE UPDATE, for each rowtripsfn_touch_updated_at
trg_create_user_walletAFTER INSERT, for each rowusersfn_create_user_wallet
trg_create_driver_availabilityAFTER INSERT, for each rowdriver_profilesfn_create_driver_availability
trg_log_trip_status_insertAFTER INSERT, for each rowtripsfn_log_trip_status
trg_log_trip_status_updateAFTER UPDATE, for each rowtripsfn_log_trip_status
trg_apply_wallet_txnBEFORE INSERT, for each rowwallet_transactionsfn_apply_wallet_txn
trg_block_update_wallet_transactionsBEFORE UPDATE, for each rowwallet_transactionsfn_block_mutation
trg_block_delete_wallet_transactionsBEFORE DELETE, for each rowwallet_transactionsfn_block_mutation
trg_block_update_audit_logsBEFORE UPDATE, for each rowaudit_logsfn_block_mutation
trg_block_delete_audit_logsBEFORE DELETE, for each rowaudit_logsfn_block_mutation
trg_block_update_trip_status_historyBEFORE UPDATE, for each rowtrip_status_historyfn_block_mutation
trg_block_delete_trip_status_historyBEFORE DELETE, for each rowtrip_status_historyfn_block_mutation
trg_apply_ratingAFTER INSERT, for each rowratingsfn_apply_rating

The trigger functions

fn_touch_updated_at()TRIGGER FUNCTION

Sets NEW.updated_at to now(), so "last changed" is always correct without the app remembering to set it.

When it runs

Before any UPDATE on users, passenger_profiles, driver_profiles, vehicles, driver_availability, wallets or trips.

Why the database is the right place

A small rule that must hold for every update from every code path. That is exactly what a trigger is for.

Which app queries make it fire

trg_touch_updated_at (BEFORE UPDATE ON users): admin.setUserStatus, admin.reinstateExpiredSuspensions, users.insert, users.markPhoneVerified, users.updateProfile, users.updatePasswordHash, users.anonymise

trg_touch_updated_at (BEFORE UPDATE ON passenger_profiles): no app query does this (the trigger exists to block it)

trg_touch_updated_at (BEFORE UPDATE ON driver_profiles): drivers.setVerificationStatus, drivers.resetRejectedToPending, vehicles.activate, vehicles.deactivate

trg_touch_updated_at (BEFORE UPDATE ON vehicles): vehicles.update, vehicles.deactivate, vehicles.resetRejectedToPending, vehicles.setVerificationStatus

trg_touch_updated_at (BEFORE UPDATE ON driver_availability): drivers.updateLocation, drivers.updateAvailability, vehicles.deactivate, zones.remove

trg_touch_updated_at (BEFORE UPDATE ON wallets): no app query does this (the trigger exists to block it)

trg_touch_updated_at (BEFORE UPDATE ON trips): disputes.markTripRefunded, trips.markArrived, trips.markStarted, trips.markCancelled, trips.completeTrip, trips.markPaid, trips.markEndedEarly, trips.markEarlyStopRequested

The code

CREATE FUNCTION fn_touch_updated_at() RETURNS TRIGGER LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
    NEW.updated_at := now();
    RETURN NEW;
END;
$$

database/schema.sql:1110

fn_log_trip_status()TRIGGER FUNCTION

Inserts a row into trip_status_history (trip, old status, new status, who). "Who" comes from current_setting('app.user_id'), which the server set with set_config at the start of the transaction.

When it runs

After a trip is inserted, and after any UPDATE of trips where the status actually changed.

Why the database is the right place

Logging sensitive changes to a history (shadow) table, exactly the checklist's example. It can't be skipped or faked by app code.

Which app queries make it fire

trg_log_trip_status_insert (AFTER INSERT ON trips): trips.insertTrip

trg_log_trip_status_update (AFTER UPDATE ON trips): disputes.markTripRefunded, trips.markArrived, trips.markStarted, trips.markCancelled, trips.completeTrip, trips.markPaid, trips.markEndedEarly, trips.markEarlyStopRequested

The code

CREATE FUNCTION fn_log_trip_status() RETURNS TRIGGER LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
DECLARE
    v_from   trip_status;
    v_actor  BIGINT;
BEGIN
    v_actor := NULLIF(current_setting('app.user_id', true), '')::BIGINT;

    IF TG_OP = 'INSERT' THEN
        v_from := NULL;
        INSERT INTO trip_status_history (trip_id, from_status, to_status, changed_by)
        VALUES (NEW.id, v_from, NEW.status, v_actor);
    ELSIF TG_OP = 'UPDATE' AND OLD.status IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.status THEN
        INSERT INTO trip_status_history (trip_id, from_status, to_status, changed_by)
        VALUES (NEW.id, OLD.status, NEW.status, v_actor);
    END IF;
    RETURN NEW;
END;
$$

database/schema.sql:1125

fn_apply_wallet_txn()TRIGGER FUNCTION

Locks the wallet row (SELECT … FOR UPDATE), adds or subtracts the amount, writes the new balance into NEW.balance_after, and updates wallets.balance.

When it runs

Before a row is inserted into wallet_transactions.

Why the database is the right place

The balance and the statement can never disagree, and two payments at the same moment are forced to take turns.

Which app queries make it fire

trg_apply_wallet_txn (BEFORE INSERT ON wallet_transactions): wallet.insertTransaction

The code

CREATE FUNCTION fn_apply_wallet_txn() RETURNS TRIGGER LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
DECLARE
    v_balance NUMERIC(12,2);
BEGIN
    SELECT balance INTO v_balance FROM wallets WHERE id = NEW.wallet_id FOR UPDATE;

    IF NEW.direction = 'credit' THEN
        v_balance := v_balance + NEW.amount;
    ELSE
        v_balance := v_balance - NEW.amount;
    END IF;

    NEW.balance_after := v_balance;

    UPDATE wallets SET balance = v_balance, updated_at = now() WHERE id = NEW.wallet_id;

    RETURN NEW;
END;
$$

Why the database is the right place

Data validation: money history, audit records and trip history must never be rewritten, even by mistake.

Which app queries make it fire

trg_block_delete_wallet_transactions (BEFORE DELETE ON wallet_transactions): no app query does this (the trigger exists to block it)

trg_block_delete_audit_logs (BEFORE DELETE ON audit_logs): no app query does this (the trigger exists to block it)

trg_block_update_trip_status_history (BEFORE UPDATE ON trip_status_history): no app query does this (the trigger exists to block it)

trg_block_delete_trip_status_history (BEFORE DELETE ON trip_status_history): no app query does this (the trigger exists to block it)

The code

CREATE FUNCTION fn_block_mutation() RETURNS TRIGGER LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
    RAISE EXCEPTION '% is append-only', TG_TABLE_NAME;
END;
$$

database/schema.sql:1178

fn_apply_rating()TRIGGER FUNCTION

Updates the rated person's rating_avg and rating_count with the formula (old average × old count + new score) ÷ (count + 1).

When it runs

After a row is inserted into ratings.

Why the database is the right place

Keeps the stored average up to date, like the checklist's "update citation count" example. (The service also recalculates it from scratch afterwards as a safety net.)

Which app queries make it fire

trg_apply_rating (AFTER INSERT ON ratings): ratings.insert

The code

CREATE FUNCTION fn_apply_rating() RETURNS TRIGGER LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
BEGIN
    IF NEW.rater_role = 'passenger' THEN
        -- passenger rated the driver
        UPDATE driver_profiles
        SET rating_avg = ((rating_avg * rating_count) + NEW.score) / (rating_count + 1),
            rating_count = rating_count + 1
        WHERE user_id = NEW.ratee_id;
    ELSE
        -- driver rated the passenger
        UPDATE passenger_profiles
        SET rating_avg = ((rating_avg * rating_count) + NEW.score) / (rating_count + 1),
            rating_count = rating_count + 1
        WHERE user_id = NEW.ratee_id;
    END IF;
    RETURN NEW;
END;
$$

Return a computed value

Functions

A function takes inputs and returns a value, and can be used inside a SELECT like a table or a column. STABLE means "same answer within one query"; IMMUTABLE means "same answer forever for the same inputs".

fn_current_pricing(p_city_id SMALLINT, p_category_id SMALLINT, p_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()FUNCTION

Returns the one price list for a city and vehicle type that is active and valid right now (newest effective_from first, LIMIT 1).

When it runs

Called from SQL in pricing.repository.getCurrentTariff: every fare quote, booking, trip completion and cancellation fee.

Why the database is the right place

A computed value the database returns. One place defines "which tariff applies", used by every query that needs it.

Called by

pricing.getCurrentTariff

The code

CREATE FUNCTION fn_current_pricing(p_city_id SMALLINT, p_category_id SMALLINT, p_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now() ) RETURNS SETOF pricing_rules LANGUAGE sql STABLE AS $$
    SELECT *
    FROM pricing_rules
    WHERE city_id = p_city_id
      AND category_id = p_category_id
      AND is_active
      AND effective_from <= p_at
      AND (effective_to IS NULL OR effective_to > p_at)
    ORDER BY effective_from DESC
    LIMIT 1;
$$

Returns SUM(credits) − SUM(debits) from wallet_transactions for one wallet.

When it runs

Not called by the app. The automated tests call it to prove the balance matches the statement; an admin could run it by hand.

Why the database is the right place

A statistic computed from many rows, returned as one value: a check that the trigger kept the balance right.

Called by

not called by the app

CREATE FUNCTION fn_wallet_balance_audit(p_wallet_id BIGINT) RETURNS NUMERIC LANGUAGE sql STABLE AS $$
    SELECT COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN direction = 'credit' THEN amount ELSE -amount END), 0)
    FROM wallet_transactions
    WHERE wallet_id = p_wallet_id;
$$

database/migrations/0003_fn_current_commission.sql:6

fn_point_in_ring(p_lat NUMERIC, p_lng NUMERIC, p_ring JSONB)FUNCTION

Returns true if a GPS point is inside a polygon, using the ray-casting method (count how many polygon edges a line from the point crosses; odd = inside).

When it runs

Called by fn_zone_at and by zones.repository.findRestrictedAt.

Why the database is the right place

A computed yes/no from the database, used inside other queries.

Called by

zones.findRestrictedAt, fn_zone_at

The code

CREATE FUNCTION fn_point_in_ring(p_lat NUMERIC, p_lng NUMERIC, p_ring JSONB) RETURNS BOOLEAN LANGUAGE plpgsql IMMUTABLE AS $$
DECLARE
    inside BOOLEAN := false;
    n INT := COALESCE(jsonb_array_length(p_ring), 0);
    i INT;
    j INT;
    xi FLOAT8; yi FLOAT8; xj FLOAT8; yj FLOAT8;
BEGIN
    IF n < 3 OR p_lat IS NULL OR p_lng IS NULL THEN RETURN false; END IF;
    j := n - 1;
    FOR i IN 0..n - 1 LOOP
        xi := (p_ring -> i ->> 0)::FLOAT8; yi := (p_ring -> i ->> 1)::FLOAT8;
        xj := (p_ring -> j ->> 0)::FLOAT8; yj := (p_ring -> j ->> 1)::FLOAT8;
        IF ((yi > p_lat) <> (yj > p_lat)) AND (p_lng < (xj - xi) * (p_lat - yi) / (yj - yi) + xi) THEN
            inside := NOT inside;
        END IF;
        j := i;
    END LOOP;
    RETURN inside;
END
$$

fn_zone_at(p_lat NUMERIC, p_lng NUMERIC, p_city_id SMALLINT DEFAULT NULL)FUNCTION

Returns the id of the zone containing a point (restricted zones win when zones overlap).

When it runs

Called inside SQL whenever a position is saved or priced: drivers.updateLocation, drivers.updateAvailability, rides.insertRequest, pricing.getActiveSurgeMultiplier.

Why the database is the right place

Lets one SQL statement save a position and tag its zone at the same time.

Called by

The code

CREATE FUNCTION fn_zone_at(p_lat NUMERIC, p_lng NUMERIC, p_city_id SMALLINT DEFAULT NULL) RETURNS BIGINT LANGUAGE sql STABLE AS $$
    SELECT id FROM zones
    WHERE is_active AND boundary_geojson IS NOT NULL
      AND (p_city_id IS NULL OR city_id = p_city_id)
      AND fn_point_in_ring(p_lat, p_lng, boundary_geojson -> 'coordinates' -> 0)
    ORDER BY (zone_type = 'restricted') DESC, id
    LIMIT 1
$$

database/migrations/0005_launch_features.sql:42

A multi-step job

Procedure

A procedure is run with CALL. It doesn't return a value like a function; it does a job that changes several tables. It hands values back through INOUT parameters. Ours runs inside the server's transaction, so the server's BEGIN / COMMIT / ROLLBACK control it.

sp_request_withdrawal(p_driver_id BIGINT, p_payout_account_id BIGINT, p_amount NUMERIC(12,2)PROCEDURE

Locks the wallet, checks the balance (RAISE EXCEPTION 'INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE' if too low), inserts the withdrawal, then inserts a debit into wallet_transactions, which fires trg_apply_wallet_txn to update the balance. Returns the new id through its INOUT parameter.

When it runs

CALLed by withdrawals.repository.request when a driver taps Withdraw (POST /driver/withdrawals), inside withTransaction.

Why the database is the right place

A multi-step workflow that changes several tables (withdrawals, wallet_transactions, wallets): exactly what the checklist says a procedure is for.

Called by

withdrawals.request

The code

CREATE PROCEDURE sp_request_withdrawal(p_driver_id BIGINT, p_payout_account_id BIGINT, p_amount NUMERIC(12,2) , p_fee NUMERIC(12,2), INOUT o_withdrawal_id BIGINT DEFAULT NULL ) LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
DECLARE
    v_wallet_id BIGINT;
    v_balance   NUMERIC(12,2);
BEGIN
    -- FOR UPDATE: a second withdrawal for the same driver waits here, so two requests can't both spend
    -- the same balance.
    SELECT id, balance INTO v_wallet_id, v_balance
    FROM wallets
    WHERE user_id = p_driver_id
    FOR UPDATE;

    IF v_balance < p_amount THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE';
    END IF;

    INSERT INTO withdrawals (driver_id, payout_account_id, amount, fee)
    VALUES (p_driver_id, p_payout_account_id, p_amount, p_fee)
    RETURNING id INTO o_withdrawal_id;

    INSERT INTO wallet_transactions
        (wallet_id, txn_type, direction, amount, reference_type, reference_id, idempotency_key)
    VALUES
        (v_wallet_id, 'withdrawal', 'debit', p_amount, 'withdrawal', o_withdrawal_id,
         'withdrawal-request-' || o_withdrawal_id);
END
$$

database/migrations/0009_sp_request_withdrawal.sql:9

How the server calls it

  1. A driver taps Withdraw on WithdrawalsPage.tsx → driverApi.requestWithdrawal() → POST /api/v1/driver/withdrawals.
  2. Guards: auth, requireRole('DRIVER'), validate(createWithdrawalSchema). Controller → withdrawals.service.requestWithdrawal checks the payout account exists and is verified.
  3. withTransaction sends BEGIN, then withdrawals.request runs CALL sp_request_withdrawal($1, $2, $3, $4, NULL).
  4. Postgres returns one row with o_withdrawal_id. The repository reads the new withdrawal back with a SELECT.
  5. COMMIT. If the procedure raised INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE, ROLLBACK instead, and the service turns it into a 422 error for the screen.
Saved SELECTs

Views

A view is a SELECT saved under a name. Queries can read it like a table.

v_active_driversVIEW

Drivers who are approved, online and have an approved active vehicle (joins 4 tables). Used by the admin dashboard's "active drivers" number.

Read by

admin.getDashboardStats

CREATE VIEW v_active_drivers AS
SELECT
    dp.user_id            AS driver_id,
    u.full_name           AS driver_name,
    u.phone                AS driver_phone,
    da.status              AS availability_status,
    da.current_lat,
    da.current_lng,
    da.current_zone_id,
    da.last_ping_at,
    v.id                   AS vehicle_id,
    v.category_id,
    v.registration_no
FROM driver_profiles dp
JOIN users u               ON u.id = dp.user_id
JOIN driver_availability da ON da.driver_id = dp.user_id
JOIN vehicles v             ON v.id = dp.active_vehicle_id
WHERE dp.verification_status = 'approved'
  AND da.status = 'online'
  AND v.verification_status = 'approved'

v_city_monthly_revenueVIEW

CREATE VIEW v_city_monthly_revenue AS
SELECT
    rr.city_id,
    date_trunc('month', t.completed_at)::date AS revenue_month,
    COUNT(*)                                  AS completed_trips,
    SUM(t.total_fare)                         AS gross_revenue,
    SUM(de.commission_amount)                 AS platform_revenue
FROM trips t
JOIN ride_requests rr   ON rr.id = t.request_id
JOIN driver_earnings de ON de.trip_id = t.id
WHERE t.status = 'completed'
GROUP BY rr.city_id, date_trunc('month', t.completed_at)

users

offers.findEligibleDrivers()READ

Dispatch: drivers who could take this ride. Joins 4 tables: online, has a GPS position, drives the right vehicle type, active account, female if women-only, not already offered this ride, and whether they are the rider's favourite.

Runs on: a timer (undefined), POST /ride-requests

The SQL

SELECT da.driver_id AS "driverId",
       da.current_lat::float8 AS "currentLat",
       da.current_lng::float8 AS "currentLng",
       EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM favorite_drivers fd
               WHERE fd.passenger_id = $4 AND fd.driver_id = da.driver_id) AS "isFavorite"
FROM driver_availability da
JOIN driver_profiles dp ON dp.user_id = da.driver_id
JOIN vehicles v ON v.id = dp.active_vehicle_id
JOIN users u ON u.id = da.driver_id
WHERE da.status = 'online'
  AND da.current_lat IS NOT NULL
  AND da.current_lng IS NOT NULL
  AND v.category_id = $1
  AND ($2 = false OR u.gender = 'female')
  AND u.status = 'active'
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ride_offers prior
                  WHERE prior.request_id = $3 AND prior.driver_id = da.driver_id)

Values sent for $1, $2…: [categoryId, womenOnly, requestId, passengerId]

Tables

favorite_drivers, driver_availability, driver_profiles, vehicles, users, ride_offers

An array of rows (an empty array if nothing matched).

offers.findPendingForDriver()READ

Driver Home: the driver's unanswered, unexpired offers with pickup, drop-off, fare and the rider's rating.

Runs on: GET /driver/offers

The SQL

SELECT
  ro.id, ro.request_id AS "requestId",
  ro.driver_distance_km::float8 AS "driverDistanceKm",
  ro.offered_at AS "offeredAt",
  ro.offered_at + ($2 * INTERVAL '1 second') AS "expiresAt",
  rr.public_id AS "requestPublicId",
  rr.pickup_address AS "pickupAddress", rr.dropoff_address AS "dropoffAddress",
  rr.est_fare::float8 AS "estFare", rr.est_distance_km::float8 AS "estDistanceKm",
  rr.est_duration_min AS "estDurationMin",
  vc.name AS "categoryName",
  pp.rating_avg AS "passengerRating"
FROM ride_offers ro
JOIN ride_requests rr ON rr.id = ro.request_id
JOIN vehicle_categories vc ON vc.id = rr.category_id
JOIN passenger_profiles pp ON pp.user_id = rr.passenger_id
WHERE ro.driver_id = $1
  AND ro.response = 'pending'
  AND ro.offered_at + ($2 * INTERVAL '1 second') > now()
ORDER BY ro.offered_at ASC

Values sent for $1, $2…: [driverId, offerTimeoutSeconds]

Tables

ride_offers, ride_requests, vehicle_categories, passenger_profiles

Returns

An array of rows (an empty array if nothing matched).

Code: return rows;

Transaction

Read-only and one statement, so it runs on its own (a single SELECT changes nothing and needs no BEGIN / COMMIT).

offers.findRequestsNeedingRedispatch()READ

Every 5 seconds: requests still searching whose last round of offers has all been answered or timed out, so the next round can go to more drivers.

Runs on: a timer (undefined)

The SQL

SELECT rr.id, rr.public_id AS "publicId", rr.passenger_id AS "passengerId",
       rr.category_id AS "categoryId", rr.women_only AS "womenOnly",
       rr.pickup_lat::float8 AS "pickupLat", rr.pickup_lng::float8 AS "pickupLng",
       COALESCE(MAX(ro.round), 0)::int AS "lastRound"
FROM ride_requests rr
LEFT JOIN ride_offers ro ON ro.request_id = rr.id
WHERE rr.status = 'searching'
GROUP BY rr.id
HAVING COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ro.response = 'pending') = 0
   AND COALESCE(MAX(ro.offered_at), rr.requested_at) + ($1 * INTERVAL '1 second') <= now()

Before booking: is the pickup or drop-off inside a restricted zone? Uses the function fn_point_in_ring.

SELECT name,
       fn_point_in_ring($2, $3, boundary_geojson -> 'coordinates' -> 0) AS "coversPickup"

trips.findByCodeForUpdate()READLOCK

Reads a trip (with its request's pickup, drop-off, prices and payment method) and LOCKS the trip row. Every trip action starts with this.

Runs on: POST /trips/:tripCode/arrived, POST /trips/:tripCode/start, POST /trips/:tripCode/stops/:stopOrder/arrived, POST /trips/:tripCode/complete, POST /trips/:tripCode/stop-request, POST /trips/:tripCode/pay, POST /trips/:tripCode/cancel

The SQL

SELECT t.id, t.trip_code AS "tripCode", t.driver_id AS "driverId",
t.passenger_id AS "passengerId", t.request_id AS "requestId", t.status,
t.assigned_at AS "assignedAt", t.arrived_at AS "arrivedAt",
t.started_at AS "startedAt", t.completed_at AS "completedAt",
t.total_fare AS "totalFare", t.payment_status AS "paymentStatus",
rr.pickup_lat::float8 AS "pickupLat", rr.pickup_lng::float8 AS "pickupLng",
rr.dropoff_lat::float8 AS "dropoffLat", rr.dropoff_lng::float8 AS "dropoffLng",
rr.city_id AS "cityId", rr.category_id AS "categoryId",
rr.payment_intent AS "paymentIntent", rr.promo_code_id AS "promoCodeId",
rr.surge_multiplier::float8 AS "surgeMultiplier", rr.stops,
t.early_stop_requested_at AS "earlyStopRequestedAt"
   FROM trips t
   JOIN ride_requests rr ON rr.id = t.request_id
   WHERE t.trip_code = $1
   FOR UPDATE OF t

trips.listForUser()READ

Trip history for a passenger or driver, newest first, one page at a time.

Runs on: GET /trips

The SQL

SELECT t.trip_code AS "publicCode", t.status,
       CASE WHEN t.passenger_id = $1 THEN 'passenger' ELSE 'driver' END AS "participantRole",
       rr.pickup_address AS "pickupAddress", rr.dropoff_address AS "dropoffAddress",
       rr.est_fare AS "estFare", t.total_fare AS "totalFare", t.currency,
       vc.name AS "categoryName",
       CASE WHEN t.passenger_id = $1 THEN du.full_name ELSE pu.full_name END AS "counterpartyName",
       t.assigned_at AS "assignedAt", t.completed_at AS "completedAt",
       count(*) OVER()::int AS "totalCount"
FROM trips t
JOIN ride_requests rr ON rr.id = t.request_id
JOIN vehicle_categories vc ON vc.id = rr.category_id
JOIN users pu ON pu.id = t.passenger_id
JOIN users du ON du.id = t.driver_id
WHERE (t.passenger_id = $1 OR t.driver_id = $1)
  AND (
    $5::text IS NULL
    OR ($5 = 'passenger' AND t.passenger_id = $1)
    OR ($5 = 'driver' AND t.driver_id = $1)
  )
  AND (
    $2::text IS NULL
    OR ($2 = 'active' AND t.status IN ('assigned', 'arrived', 'in_progress'))
    OR t.status::text = $2
  )
ORDER BY t.created_at DESC
LIMIT $3 OFFSET $4

Values sent for $1, $2…: [userId, status ?? null, limit, offset, role ?? null]

Tables

trips, ride_requests, vehicle_categories, users

Returns

An array of rows (an empty array if nothing matched).

Code: return rows;

Transaction

Read-only and one statement, so it runs on its own (a single SELECT changes nothing and needs no BEGIN / COMMIT).

trips.findDetailForUser()READ

Everything about one trip for its receipt / details page: people, vehicle, times, fare, cancellation, receipt, your rating, stops, favourite and report flags.

Runs on: GET /trips/:tripCode

The SQL

SELECT t.id, t.trip_code AS "publicCode", t.status,
       CASE WHEN t.passenger_id = $2 THEN 'passenger' ELSE 'driver' END AS "participantRole",
       rr.public_id AS "requestPublicId", rr.pickup_lat::float8 AS "pickupLat",
       rr.pickup_lng::float8 AS "pickupLng", rr.pickup_address AS "pickupAddress",
       rr.dropoff_lat::float8 AS "dropoffLat", rr.dropoff_lng::float8 AS "dropoffLng",
       rr.dropoff_address AS "dropoffAddress", rr.est_distance_km::float8 AS "estDistanceKm",
       rr.est_duration_min AS "estDurationMin", rr.est_fare AS "estFare",
       rr.surge_multiplier AS "surgeMultiplier", rr.payment_intent AS "paymentIntent",
       c.name AS "cityName", vc.name AS "categoryName",
       pu.public_id AS "passengerPublicId", pu.full_name AS "passengerName",
       pu.phone AS "passengerPhone", pu.photo_url AS "passengerPhotoUrl",
       pp.rating_avg AS "passengerRating",
       du.public_id AS "driverPublicId", du.full_name AS "driverName",
       du.phone AS "driverPhone", du.photo_url AS "driverPhotoUrl",
       dp.rating_avg AS "driverRating",
       v.registration_no AS "vehicleRegistrationNo", v.brand AS "vehicleBrand",
       v.model AS "vehicleModel", v.color AS "vehicleColor",
       t.assigned_at AS "assignedAt", t.arrived_at AS "arrivedAt",
       t.started_at AS "startedAt", t.completed_at AS "completedAt",
       t.actual_distance_km::float8 AS "actualDistanceKm",
       t.actual_duration_min AS "actualDurationMin",
       t.base_fare AS "baseFare", t.distance_fare AS "distanceFare",
       t.time_fare AS "timeFare", t.waiting_fare AS "waitingFare",
       t.surge_amount AS "surgeAmount", t.booking_fee AS "bookingFee",
       t.discount_amount AS "discountAmount", t.total_fare AS "totalFare",
       t.currency, t.payment_status AS "paymentStatus",
       tc.cancelled_by_role AS "cancelledByRole", tc.reason_code AS "cancellationReasonCode",
       tc.reason_text AS "cancellationReasonText", tc.fee_charged AS "cancellationFee",
       tc.cancelled_at AS "cancelledAt",
       r.receipt_no AS "receiptNo", r.issued_at AS "receiptIssuedAt",
       (SELECT jsonb_build_object('score', rt.score, 'comment', rt.comment)
        FROM ratings rt WHERE rt.trip_id = t.id AND rt.rater_id = $2) AS "myRating",
       (SELECT COALESCE(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
                 'order', ts.stop_order, 'lat', ts.lat::float8, 'lng', ts.lng::float8,
                 'address', ts.address_text, 'arrivedAt', ts.arrived_at) ORDER BY ts.stop_order), '[]'::jsonb)
        FROM trip_stops ts WHERE ts.trip_id = t.id) AS stops,
       EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM favorite_drivers fd
               WHERE fd.passenger_id = $2 AND fd.driver_id = t.driver_id) AS "driverIsFavorite",
       EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM user_reports ur
               WHERE ur.trip_id = t.id AND ur.reporter_id = $2) AS "reportedByMe",
       t.ended_early_at AS "endedEarlyAt", t.end_lat::float8 AS "endLat", t.end_lng::float8 AS "endLng",
       t.early_stop_requested_at AS "earlyStopRequestedAt"
FROM trips t
JOIN ride_requests rr ON rr.id = t.request_id
JOIN cities c ON c.id = rr.city_id
JOIN vehicle_categories vc ON vc.id = rr.category_id
JOIN users pu ON pu.id = t.passenger_id
JOIN passenger_profiles pp ON pp.user_id = t.passenger_id
JOIN users du ON du.id = t.driver_id
JOIN driver_profiles dp ON dp.user_id = t.driver_id
JOIN vehicles v ON v.id = t.vehicle_id
LEFT JOIN trip_cancellations tc ON tc.trip_id = t.id
LEFT JOIN receipts r ON r.trip_id = t.id
WHERE t.trip_code = $1 AND (t.passenger_id = $2 OR t.driver_id = $2)

Values sent for $1, $2…: [tripCode, userId]

trips.findLatestLocationForUser()READ

The driver's latest position for a trip (last ping, or the live position if no ping yet).

Runs on: GET /trips/:tripCode/track

The SQL

SELECT COALESCE(p.lat, da.current_lat)::float8 AS lat,
       COALESCE(p.lng, da.current_lng)::float8 AS lng,
       COALESCE(p.heading, da.heading)::float8 AS heading,
       COALESCE(p.recorded_at, da.last_ping_at) AS at
FROM trips t
JOIN driver_availability da ON da.driver_id = t.driver_id
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT lat, lng, heading, recorded_at
  FROM trip_location_pings
  WHERE trip_id = t.id
  ORDER BY recorded_at DESC
  LIMIT 1
) p ON true
WHERE t.trip_code = $1 AND (t.passenger_id = $2 OR t.driver_id = $2)

trips.listMessages()READ

The trip chat messages with sender names.

Runs on: GET /trips/:tripCode/messages

The SQL

SELECT tm.id, u.public_id AS "senderId", u.full_name AS "senderName",
       u.photo_url AS "senderPhotoUrl", tm.message_type AS "messageType",
       tm.body, tm.sent_at AS "sentAt", tm.read_at AS "readAt"
FROM trip_messages tm
JOIN users u ON u.id = tm.sender_id
WHERE tm.trip_id = $1

trips.findSharedView()READ

The public "follow my ride" page data for a share link: first names only, car, route and status.

Runs on: GET /share/:token

The SQL

SELECT t.trip_code AS "tripCode", t.status, t.assigned_at AS "assignedAt",
       t.started_at AS "startedAt", t.completed_at AS "completedAt",
       GREATEST(t.completed_at, tc.cancelled_at) AS "endedAt",
       split_part(du.full_name, ' ', 1) AS "driverFirstName", du.photo_url AS "driverPhotoUrl",
       dp.rating_avg AS "driverRating",
       v.registration_no AS "registrationNo", v.brand, v.model, v.color,
       rr.pickup_address AS "pickupAddress", rr.dropoff_address AS "dropoffAddress",
       rr.pickup_lat::float8 AS "pickupLat", rr.pickup_lng::float8 AS "pickupLng",
       rr.dropoff_lat::float8 AS "dropoffLat", rr.dropoff_lng::float8 AS "dropoffLng",
       COALESCE(rr.stops, '[]'::jsonb) AS stops,
       loc.lat, loc.lng, loc.at AS "locationAt"
FROM trips t
JOIN ride_requests rr ON rr.id = t.request_id
JOIN users du ON du.id = t.driver_id
JOIN driver_profiles dp ON dp.user_id = t.driver_id
JOIN vehicles v ON v.id = t.vehicle_id
JOIN driver_availability da ON da.driver_id = t.driver_id
LEFT JOIN trip_cancellations tc ON tc.trip_id = t.id
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT COALESCE(p.lat, da.current_lat)::float8 AS lat, COALESCE(p.lng, da.current_lng)::float8 AS lng,
         COALESCE(p.recorded_at, da.last_ping_at) AS at
  FROM (SELECT 1) one
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (SELECT lat, lng, recorded_at FROM trip_location_pings
                     WHERE trip_id = t.id ORDER BY recorded_at DESC LIMIT 1) p ON true
) loc ON t.status IN ('assigned', 'arrived', 'in_progress')
WHERE t.id = $1

Values sent for $1, $2…: [tripId]

Tables

trips, ride_requests, users, driver_profiles, vehicles, driver_availability, trip_cancellations, trip_location_pings

Returns

One row as a JavaScript object, or undefined if nothing matched.

Code: return rows[0];

Transaction

Read-only and one statement, so it runs on its own (a single SELECT changes nothing and needs no BEGIN / COMMIT).

social.listReports()READ

The admin Reports page with reporter and reported user packed as JSON.

Runs on: GET /admin/reports

The SQL

SELECT ur.id, ur.category, ur.description, ur.status, ur.created_at AS "createdAt",
       ur.resolved_at AS "resolvedAt", t.trip_code AS "tripCode",
       jsonb_build_object('id', rep.id, 'name', rep.full_name, 'phone', rep.phone) AS reporter,
       jsonb_build_object('id', red.id, 'name', red.full_name, 'phone', red.phone, 'status', red.status,
                          'openReports', (SELECT count(*)::int FROM user_reports o
                                          WHERE o.reported_id = red.id AND o.status IN ('open', 'investigating')))
         AS reported,
       count(*) OVER()::int AS "totalCount"
FROM user_reports ur
JOIN users rep ON rep.id = ur.reporter_id
JOIN users red ON red.id = ur.reported_id
LEFT JOIN trips t ON t.id = ur.trip_id
WHERE ($1::report_status IS NULL OR ur.status = $1)
ORDER BY (ur.status IN ('open', 'investigating')) DESC, ur.created_at DESC
LIMIT $2 OFFSET $3

documents.expireLapsedDocuments()UPDATE

Nightly: marks every approved driver or vehicle document past its expiry date as "expired" (two UPDATEs inside a WITH block) and returns which drivers were affected so they can be told.

Runs on: a timer (undefined)

The SQL

WITH driver_docs AS (
  UPDATE driver_documents SET status = 'expired'
  WHERE status = 'approved' AND expiry_date < CURRENT_DATE
  RETURNING driver_id, doc_type::text
), vehicle_docs AS (
  UPDATE vehicle_documents vd SET status = 'expired'
  FROM vehicles v
  WHERE v.id = vd.vehicle_id AND vd.status = 'approved' AND vd.expiry_date < CURRENT_DATE
  RETURNING v.driver_id, vd.doc_type::text
)
SELECT driver_id AS "driverId", doc_type AS "docType" FROM driver_docs
UNION ALL SELECT driver_id, doc_type FROM vehicle_docs

earnings.getStatementForMonth()READ

One monthly statement: driver details plus every trip of that month packed into a JSON list.

Runs on: GET /driver/statements/:month

The SQL

SELECT u.full_name AS "driverName", u.phone AS "driverPhone", dp.license_number AS "licenseNumber",
       (SELECT COALESCE(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
                 'tripCode', t.trip_code, 'earnedAt', de.earned_at, 'grossFare', de.gross_fare::float8,
                 'commissionPct', de.commission_pct::float8, 'commissionAmount', de.commission_amount::float8,
                 'netEarning', de.net_earning::float8, 'paymentMethod', rr.payment_intent)
               ORDER BY de.earned_at), '[]'::jsonb)
        FROM driver_earnings de
        JOIN trips t ON t.id = de.trip_id
        JOIN ride_requests rr ON rr.id = t.request_id
        WHERE de.driver_id = $1 AND date_trunc('month', de.earned_at) = to_date($2, 'YYYY-MM')::timestamptz
       ) AS trips
FROM users u JOIN driver_profiles dp ON dp.user_id = u.id
WHERE u.id = $1

Values sent for $1, $2…: [driverId, month]

driver_earnings, trips, ride_requests, users, driver_profiles

wallet.getByUserIdForUpdate()READLOCK

A user's wallet, LOCKED, before checking the balance and spending from it. Stops two payments spending the same money.

Runs on: POST /trips/:tripCode/pay

The SQL

SELECT id, user_id AS "userId", balance, currency, status
FROM wallets
WHERE user_id = $1
FOR UPDATE

Values sent for $1, $2…: [userId]

Tables

wallets

Returns

One row as a JavaScript object, or undefined if nothing matched.

Code: return rows[0];

Transaction

Must run inside a transaction: a lock (FOR UPDATE / advisory lock) only lasts until COMMIT or ROLLBACK, so it is always called with the transaction's client.

wallet.insertTransaction()INSERT

Adds one line to the wallet statement. This INSERT fires trg_apply_wallet_txn, which updates the wallet balance. idempotency_key is UNIQUE, so the same money movement can never be recorded twice.

Runs on: POST /admin/disputes/:id/resolve, ALL /payments/:publicId/return, POST /webhooks/payments/:gateway, POST /trips/:tripCode/complete, POST /trips/:tripCode/pay, POST /admin/withdrawals/:id/reject

The SQL

INSERT INTO wallet_transactions
  (wallet_id, txn_type, direction, amount, reference_type, reference_id, idempotency_key, note)
VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, $7, $8)
RETURNING id, balance_after AS "balanceAfter", created_at AS "createdAt"

Values sent for $1, $2…: [walletId, txnType, direction, amount, referenceType, referenceId ?? null, idempotencyKey, note ?? null]

Tables

wallet_transactions

Returns

The new row as a JavaScript object: the columns listed after RETURNING.

Code: return rows[0];

Transaction

Always inside a transaction. The caller opened BEGIN with withTransaction and passes its client in. If anything later fails, ROLLBACK undoes this change too; otherwise COMMIT saves it.

          purpose, method_type AS "methodType", amount, status, completed_at AS "completedAt"

The admin SOS board with who raised each alert and the trip.

Runs on: GET /admin/sos

The SQL

SELECT sa.id, sa.status, sa.lat::float8 AS lat, sa.lng::float8 AS lng,
       sa.triggered_at AS "triggeredAt", sa.resolved_at AS "resolvedAt",
       sa.resolution_note AS "resolutionNote", u.full_name AS "triggeredByName",
       u.phone AS "triggeredByPhone", t.trip_code AS "tripCode",
       au.full_name AS "acknowledgedByName",
       lp.lat::float8 AS "liveLat", lp.lng::float8 AS "liveLng", lp.recorded_at AS "liveAt",
       count(*) OVER()::int AS "totalCount"
FROM sos_alerts sa JOIN users u ON u.id = sa.triggered_by
LEFT JOIN trips t ON t.id = sa.trip_id LEFT JOIN users au ON au.id = sa.acknowledged_by
LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT p.lat, p.lng, p.recorded_at FROM trip_location_pings p
  WHERE p.trip_id = sa.trip_id ORDER BY p.recorded_at DESC LIMIT 1
) lp ON true
WHERE ($1::text IS NULL OR sa.status::text = $1)
ORDER BY CASE WHEN sa.status = 'active' THEN 0 WHEN sa.status = 'acknowledged' THEN 1 ELSE 2 END,
         sa.triggered_at DESC LIMIT $2 OFFSET $3

Values sent for $1, $2…: [status ?? null, limit, offset]

Tables

sos_alerts, users, trips, trip_location_pings

Returns

An array of rows (an empty array if nothing matched).

Code: return rows;

Transaction

Read-only and one statement, so it runs on its own (a single SELECT changes nothing and needs no BEGIN / COMMIT).

Changes a ticket's status, priority or assignee. COALESCE keeps fields that weren't sent.

Runs on: PATCH /admin/support/tickets/:id, POST /admin/support/tickets/:id/messages

The SQL

UPDATE support_tickets SET
  status = COALESCE($2, status), priority = COALESCE($3, priority),
  assigned_to = CASE WHEN $4::boolean THEN $5 ELSE assigned_to END,
  resolved_at = CASE WHEN $2 = 'resolved' THEN now() WHEN $2 IS NOT NULL THEN NULL ELSE resolved_at END,
  closed_at = CASE WHEN $2 = 'closed' THEN now() WHEN $2 IS NOT NULL THEN NULL ELSE closed_at END
WHERE id = $1
RETURNING id, ticket_no AS "ticketNo", status, priority, assigned_to AS "assignedTo",
          resolved_at AS "resolvedAt", closed_at AS "closedAt"

Runs on: POST /admin/users/:id/suspend, POST /admin/users/:id/reinstate, POST /admin/documents/:id/review, POST /admin/vehicle-documents/:id/review, POST /admin/drivers/:id/approve, POST /admin/drivers/:id/reject, POST /admin/vehicles/:id/approve, POST /admin/vehicles/:id/reject, POST /admin/disputes/:id/resolve, POST /admin/disputes/:id/review, PATCH /admin/reports/:id, POST /trips/:tripCode/complete, a timer (undefined), POST /admin/support/tickets/:id/messages, POST /trips/:tripCode/stop-request

notifications.listForUser()READ

The Notifications page, newest first, one page at a time, with the total count.

Runs on: GET /notifications

The SQL

SELECT id, category, title, body, payload, read_at AS "readAt", created_at AS "createdAt",
       count(*) OVER()::int AS "totalCount"
FROM notifications WHERE user_id = $1
ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT $2 OFFSET $3

Values sent for $1, $2…: [userId, limit, (page - 1) * limit]

Tables

notifications

Returns

An array of rows (an empty array if nothing matched).

Code: return rows;

Transaction

Read-only and one statement, so it runs on its own (a single SELECT changes nothing and needs no BEGIN / COMMIT).

admin.listDriverApplications()READ

The driver-approval queue: drivers with a given status plus the newest copy of each of their documents (DISTINCT ON keeps only the latest per type), with a total count for paging.

Runs on: GET /admin/drivers

The SQL

WITH latest_documents AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (driver_id, doc_type)
         id, driver_id, doc_type, status, expiry_date, uploaded_at,
         file_url, doc_number, rejection_reason
  FROM driver_documents
  ORDER BY driver_id, doc_type, uploaded_at DESC, id DESC
)
SELECT dp.user_id AS id, u.public_id AS "publicId",
       u.full_name AS "fullName", u.phone,
       dp.nid_number AS "nidNumber", dp.license_number AS "licenseNumber",
       dp.license_expiry::text AS "licenseExpiry",
       dp.verification_status AS "verificationStatus",
       dp.created_at AS "appliedAt",
       COUNT(*) OVER()::int AS "totalCount",
       COALESCE(
         jsonb_agg(
           jsonb_build_object(
             'id', ld.id,
             'docType', ld.doc_type,
             'status', ld.status,
             'expiryDate', ld.expiry_date,
             'fileUrl', ld.file_url,
             'docNumber', ld.doc_number,
             'rejectionReason', ld.rejection_reason
           ) ORDER BY ld.doc_type
         ) FILTER (WHERE ld.id IS NOT NULL),
         '[]'::jsonb
       ) AS documents
FROM driver_profiles dp
JOIN users u ON u.id = dp.user_id
LEFT JOIN latest_documents ld ON ld.driver_id = dp.user_id
WHERE dp.verification_status = $1
GROUP BY dp.user_id, u.public_id, u.full_name, u.phone,
         dp.nid_number, dp.license_number, dp.license_expiry,
         dp.verification_status, dp.created_at
ORDER BY dp.created_at ASC, dp.user_id ASC
LIMIT $2 OFFSET $3

Values sent for $1, $2…: [status, limit, offset]

Tables

driver_documents, driver_profiles, users

Returns

An object with the rows and the total count (for paging).

Code: return {

Transaction

Read-only and one statement, so it runs on its own (a single SELECT changes nothing and needs no BEGIN / COMMIT).

admin.getDashboardStats()READ

One row with 8 numbers for the admin dashboard: trips today, active drivers (from the view v_active_drivers), pending drivers, withdrawal requests, open disputes, live SOS, and this month's revenue (from the view v_city_monthly_revenue). Each number is its own small sub-query.

Runs on: GET /admin/stats

The SQL

SELECT
(SELECT count(*)::int
   FROM trips t JOIN ride_requests rr ON rr.id = t.request_id
  WHERE t.assigned_at >= date_trunc('day', now() AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Dhaka') AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Dhaka'
    AND ($1::smallint IS NULL OR rr.city_id = $1)) AS "tripsToday",
(SELECT count(*)::int FROM v_active_drivers vad
  WHERE ($1::smallint IS NULL OR vad.current_zone_id IN (SELECT id FROM zones WHERE city_id = $1))) AS "activeDrivers",
(SELECT count(*)::int FROM driver_profiles WHERE verification_status = 'pending') AS "pendingDrivers",
(SELECT count(*)::int FROM withdrawals WHERE status = 'requested') AS "requestedWithdrawals",
(SELECT count(*)::int FROM disputes WHERE status IN ('open', 'under_review')) AS "openDisputes",
(SELECT count(*)::int FROM sos_alerts WHERE status IN ('active', 'acknowledged')) AS "openSos",
COALESCE((SELECT sum(gross_revenue) FROM v_city_monthly_revenue
  WHERE revenue_month = date_trunc('month', now())::date
    AND ($1::smallint IS NULL OR city_id = $1)), 0) AS "grossRevenueMonth",
COALESCE((SELECT sum(platform_revenue) FROM v_city_monthly_revenue
  WHERE revenue_month = date_trunc('month', now())::date
    AND ($1::smallint IS NULL OR city_id = $1)), 0) AS "platformRevenueMonth"

Values sent for $1, $2…: [cityId ?? null]

trips, ride_requests, v_active_drivers, zones, driver_profiles, withdrawals, disputes, sos_alerts, v_city_monthly_revenue

admin.getRevenueTrend()READ

The last 6 months of revenue for the dashboard chart. It builds a list of 6 months and LEFT JOINs the revenue view, so a month with no trips still shows 0.

Runs on: GET /admin/stats

The SQL

WITH months AS (
  SELECT generate_series(
    date_trunc('month', now()) - interval '5 months',
    date_trunc('month', now()), interval '1 month'
  )::date AS month
)
SELECT m.month::text,
       COALESCE(sum(v.completed_trips), 0)::int AS "completedTrips",
       COALESCE(sum(v.gross_revenue), 0) AS "grossRevenue",
       COALESCE(sum(v.platform_revenue), 0) AS "platformRevenue"
FROM months m
LEFT JOIN v_city_monthly_revenue v
  ON v.revenue_month = m.month AND ($1::smallint IS NULL OR v.city_id = $1)
GROUP BY m.month
ORDER BY m.month

admin.getTopDrivers()READ

Top 10 drivers by completed trips (ties broken by earnings) since a date, optionally in one city. Joins 5 tables and uses COUNT and SUM with GROUP BY.

Runs on: GET /admin/leaderboard

The SQL

SELECT u.public_id AS "publicId",
       u.full_name AS "name",
       u.phone,
       COUNT(*) AS "completedTrips",
       COALESCE(SUM(e.net_earning), 0) AS "netEarned",
       COALESCE(SUM(t.actual_distance_km), 0) AS "distanceKm",
       d.rating_avg AS "rating",
       d.rating_count AS "ratingCount"
FROM trips t
JOIN ride_requests r ON r.id = t.request_id
JOIN users u ON u.id = t.driver_id
JOIN driver_profiles d ON d.user_id = t.driver_id
LEFT JOIN driver_earnings e ON e.trip_id = t.id
WHERE t.status = 'completed'
  AND u.status <> 'deleted'
  AND t.completed_at >= $1
  AND r.city_id = COALESCE($2, r.city_id)
GROUP BY u.id, u.public_id, u.full_name, u.phone, d.rating_avg, d.rating_count
ORDER BY "completedTrips" DESC, "netEarned" DESC
FETCH FIRST 10 ROWS ONLY

admin.listUsers()READ

The admin Users page: every user with wallet balance, their roles collected into a list, and trip count. Supports searching by name, phone or email and filtering by status, one page at a time.

Runs on: GET /admin/users

The SQL

SELECT u.id, u.public_id AS "publicId", u.full_name AS "fullName", u.phone,
       u.email, u.status, u.created_at AS "createdAt", u.last_login_at AS "lastLoginAt",
       u.suspended_until AS "suspendedUntil", u.suspension_reason AS "suspensionReason",
       w.balance AS "walletBalance", w.currency,
       COALESCE(array_agg(r.name ORDER BY r.name) FILTER (WHERE r.name IS NOT NULL), '{}') AS roles,
       (SELECT count(*)::int FROM trips t WHERE t.passenger_id = u.id OR t.driver_id = u.id) AS "tripCount",
       count(*) OVER()::int AS "totalCount"
FROM users u
JOIN wallets w ON w.user_id = u.id
LEFT JOIN user_roles ur ON ur.user_id = u.id
LEFT JOIN roles r ON r.id = ur.role_id
WHERE ($1 = '' OR u.full_name ILIKE $2 OR u.phone ILIKE $2 OR COALESCE(u.email, '') ILIKE $2)
  AND ($3::text IS NULL OR u.status::text = $3)
GROUP BY u.id, w.balance, w.currency
ORDER BY u.created_at DESC, u.id DESC
LIMIT $4 OFFSET $5

admin.listVehicleApplications()READ

The vehicle-approval queue: vehicles with the driver's name and the newest copy of each vehicle document packed into a JSON list.

Runs on: GET /admin/vehicles

The SQL

WITH latest_documents AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT ON (vehicle_id, doc_type) *
  FROM vehicle_documents
  ORDER BY vehicle_id, doc_type, uploaded_at DESC, id DESC
)
SELECT v.id, v.driver_id AS "driverId", u.full_name AS "driverName", u.phone AS "driverPhone",
       v.registration_no AS "registrationNo", v.brand, v.model, v.model_year AS "modelYear",
       v.color, vc.name AS "categoryName", v.verification_status AS "verificationStatus",
       v.created_at AS "createdAt", count(*) OVER()::int AS "totalCount",
       COALESCE(jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
         'id', ld.id, 'docType', ld.doc_type, 'status', ld.status,
         'expiryDate', ld.expiry_date, 'fileUrl', ld.file_url,
         'docNumber', ld.doc_number, 'rejectionReason', ld.rejection_reason
       ) ORDER BY ld.doc_type) FILTER (WHERE ld.id IS NOT NULL), '[]'::jsonb) AS documents
FROM vehicles v
JOIN users u ON u.id = v.driver_id
JOIN vehicle_categories vc ON vc.id = v.category_id
LEFT JOIN latest_documents ld ON ld.vehicle_id = v.id
WHERE v.verification_status = $1
GROUP BY v.id, u.full_name, u.phone, vc.name
ORDER BY v.created_at ASC, v.id ASC
LIMIT $2 OFFSET $3

marketplace.listPromos()READ

The admin Promo codes page, with how many times each code has been used.

Runs on: GET /admin/promos

The SQL

SELECT p.id, p.code, p.description, p.promo_type AS "promoType", p.value::float8 AS value,
p.max_discount::float8 AS "maxDiscount", p.min_fare::float8 AS "minFare",
p.usage_limit_total AS "usageLimitTotal", p.usage_limit_per_user AS "usageLimitPerUser",
p.first_ride_only AS "firstRideOnly", p.city_id AS "cityId", p.category_id AS "categoryId",
p.valid_from AS "validFrom", p.valid_until AS "validUntil", p.is_active AS "isActive",
p.created_at AS "createdAt",
(SELECT count(*)::int FROM promo_redemptions pr WHERE pr.promo_code_id = p.id) AS "redemptions",

marketplace.exportRows()READ

The CSV downloads on the dashboard. Depending on "kind" it runs one of three big SELECTs (trips joined with 6 tables, payments, or withdrawals) for a date range.

Runs on: GET /admin/exports/:kind.csv

The SQL

-- kind = 'trips'
SELECT t.trip_code AS "tripCode", t.status, c.name AS city, vc.name AS category,
           to_char(t.assigned_at, 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI') AS "assignedAt",
           to_char(t.completed_at, 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI') AS "completedAt",
           t.actual_distance_km AS "distanceKm", t.actual_duration_min AS "durationMin",
           t.total_fare AS "totalFare", t.discount_amount AS discount, t.surge_amount AS surge,
           rr.payment_intent AS "paymentMethod", t.payment_status AS "paymentStatus",
           de.commission_amount AS commission, de.net_earning AS "driverEarning",
           pu.phone AS "passengerPhone", du.phone AS "driverPhone"
    FROM trips t
    JOIN ride_requests rr ON rr.id = t.request_id
    JOIN cities c ON c.id = rr.city_id
    JOIN vehicle_categories vc ON vc.id = rr.category_id
    JOIN users pu ON pu.id = t.passenger_id
    JOIN users du ON du.id = t.driver_id
    LEFT JOIN driver_earnings de ON de.trip_id = t.id
    WHERE t.assigned_at >= $1::date AND t.assigned_at < $2::date + 1
    ORDER BY t.assigned_at

Values sent for $1, $2…: [from, to]

-- kind = 'payments'
SELECT p.public_id AS "paymentId", p.purpose, p.method_type AS method, p.gateway, p.status,
           p.amount, to_char(p.initiated_at, 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI') AS "initiatedAt",
           to_char(p.completed_at, 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI') AS "completedAt",
           t.trip_code AS "tripCode", u.phone AS "payerPhone", p.gateway_txn_id AS "gatewayTxnId"
    FROM payments p
    JOIN users u ON u.id = p.payer_id
    LEFT JOIN trips t ON t.id = p.trip_id
    WHERE p.initiated_at >= $1::date AND p.initiated_at < $2::date + 1
    ORDER BY p.initiated_at

Values sent for $1, $2…: [from, to]

-- kind = 'withdrawals'
SELECT w.id, u.full_name AS driver, u.phone AS "driverPhone", w.amount, w.fee, w.status,
           pa.account_type AS "accountType", pa.account_no_masked AS "accountNumber", w.gateway_ref AS "reference",
           to_char(w.requested_at, 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI') AS "requestedAt",
           to_char(w.processed_at, 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI') AS "processedAt"
    FROM withdrawals w
    JOIN users u ON u.id = w.driver_id
    JOIN driver_payout_accounts pa ON pa.id = w.payout_account_id
    WHERE w.requested_at >= $1::date AND w.requested_at < $2::date + 1
    ORDER BY w.requested_at

audit.list()READ

The Audit log page: log lines with the admin's name, newest first, filterable, one page at a time.

Runs on: GET /admin/audit-logs

The SQL

SELECT al.id, al.actor_id AS "actorId", u.full_name AS "actorName",
       al.actor_role AS "actorRole", al.action, al.entity_type AS "entityType",
       al.entity_id AS "entityId", al.old_value AS "oldValue",
       al.new_value AS "newValue", host(al.ip_address) AS "ipAddress",
       al.created_at AS "createdAt", count(*) OVER()::int AS "totalCount"
FROM audit_logs al
LEFT JOIN users u ON u.id = al.actor_id
WHERE ($1::text IS NULL OR al.entity_type = $1)
  AND ($2::bigint IS NULL OR al.actor_id = $2)
  AND ($3::text IS NULL OR al.action ILIKE '%' || $3 || '%')
ORDER BY al.created_at DESC, al.id DESC
LIMIT $4 OFFSET $5

Values sent for $1, $2…: [entityType ?? null, actorId ?? null, action ?? null, limit, offset]

Tables

audit_logs, users

Returns

An array of rows (an empty array if nothing matched).

Code: return rows;

Transaction

Read-only and one statement, so it runs on its own (a single SELECT changes nothing and needs no BEGIN / COMMIT).

Admin Analytics page

The 10 analytics reports

These ten SQL texts live in one list, REPORTS, and are all run by analytics.runReport.

#9 Peak ride hourREAD

At which hour of the day do riders request the most rides?

Runs on: GET /admin/analytics (admin Analytics page)

 
SELECT EXTRACT(HOUR FROM r.requested_at) AS hour_of_day,
       COUNT(*) AS total_requests
FROM ride_requests r
GROUP BY EXTRACT(HOUR FROM r.requested_at)
ORDER BY total_requests DESC
FETCH FIRST 5 ROWS ONLY

#10 Highest revenue hourREAD

At which hour of the day do completed trips bring in the most money?

Runs on: GET /admin/analytics (admin Analytics page)

 
SELECT EXTRACT(HOUR FROM t.completed_at) AS hour_of_day,
       COUNT(*) AS completed_trips,
       SUM(t.total_fare) AS total_revenue
FROM trips t
WHERE t.status = 'completed'
GROUP BY EXTRACT(HOUR FROM t.completed_at)
ORDER BY total_revenue DESC
FETCH FIRST 5 ROWS ONLY

#11 Highest revenue day of the monthREAD

In the chosen month, which days had the most successful trip payments?

Runs on: GET /admin/analytics (admin Analytics page)

 
SELECT TO_CHAR(p.completed_at, 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS payment_day,
       COUNT(*) AS payments,
       SUM(p.amount) AS total_amount
FROM payments p
WHERE p.status = 'succeeded'
  AND p.purpose = 'trip'
  AND TO_CHAR(p.completed_at, 'YYYY-MM') = $1
GROUP BY TO_CHAR(p.completed_at, 'YYYY-MM-DD')
ORDER BY total_amount DESC
FETCH FIRST 5 ROWS ONLY

#12 Monthly revenue trendREAD

For each month: how many trips, how much money, the average fare, and how many different riders?

Runs on: GET /admin/analytics (admin Analytics page)

 
SELECT TO_CHAR(t.completed_at, 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
       COUNT(*) AS completed_trips,
       SUM(t.total_fare) AS gross_revenue,
       ROUND(AVG(t.total_fare), 2) AS average_fare,
       COUNT(DISTINCT t.passenger_id) AS different_riders
FROM trips t
WHERE t.status = 'completed'
GROUP BY TO_CHAR(t.completed_at, 'YYYY-MM')
ORDER BY month DESC
FETCH FIRST 12 ROWS ONLY

#3 Top 5 drivers by ratingREAD

Who are the 5 best-rated drivers, counting only drivers with at least the minimum number of trips?

Runs on: GET /admin/analytics (admin Analytics page)

 
SELECT u.full_name AS driver_name,
       COUNT(t.id) AS completed_trips,
       ROUND(AVG(r.score), 2) AS average_rating
FROM trips t
JOIN users u ON u.id = t.driver_id
LEFT JOIN ratings r ON r.trip_id = t.id
                   AND r.rater_role = 'passenger'
WHERE t.status = 'completed'
GROUP BY u.id, u.full_name
HAVING COUNT(t.id) >= $1
ORDER BY average_rating DESC NULLS LAST, completed_trips DESC
FETCH FIRST 5 ROWS ONLY

#17 Online drivers with no ride todayREAD

Which drivers are online right now but have not been given a single trip today?

WHERE a.status = 'online'
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1

#18 Inactive driversREAD

Which approved drivers have not completed any trip in the last 30 days?

Runs on: GET /admin/analytics (admin Analytics page)

 
SELECT u.full_name AS driver_name,
       u.phone,
       (SELECT TO_CHAR(MAX(t2.completed_at), 'YYYY-MM-DD')

#20 Rider lifetime valueREAD

For each rider: total trips, total spent, average fare, and their first and latest trip.

Runs on: GET /admin/analytics (admin Analytics page)

 
SELECT u.full_name AS rider_name,
       COUNT(*) AS total_trips,
       SUM(t.total_fare) AS total_spent,
       ROUND(AVG(t.total_fare), 2) AS average_fare,
       TO_CHAR(MIN(t.completed_at), 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS first_trip,
       TO_CHAR(MAX(t.completed_at), 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS latest_trip
FROM trips t
JOIN users u ON u.id = t.passenger_id
WHERE t.status = 'completed'
GROUP BY u.id, u.full_name
ORDER BY total_spent DESC
FETCH FIRST 10 ROWS ONLY

#21 Most frequent driver–rider pairREAD

Which driver and rider have completed the most trips together?

Runs on: GET /admin/analytics (admin Analytics page)

 
SELECT d.full_name AS driver_name,
       p.full_name AS rider_name,
       COUNT(*) AS trips_together
FROM trips t
JOIN users d ON d.id = t.driver_id
JOIN users p ON p.id = t.passenger_id
WHERE t.status = 'completed'
GROUP BY d.id, d.full_name, p.id, p.full_name
ORDER BY trips_together DESC
FETCH FIRST 5 ROWS ONLY

FROM user_roles ur JOIN roles r ON r.id = ur.role_id JOIN users u ON u.id = ur.user_id
WHERE r.name = 'ADMIN' AND u.status = 'active'
